attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post, endorsed.

semantics.note: The relative clause 'that will emerge' firmly commits him to open-source Sora counterparts appearing, so this is a scored forecast. Dropping 'in short order' is defensible, and it changes nothing here: Open-Sora 1.0 shipped within a month of the post.

contract.note: The plain reading is fair and ordinary: public text-to-video models with downloadable weights, runnable code and an open license, without requiring parity with Sora. If parity were required, this packet would not settle the claim.

evidence.note: Official repo entry dated 2024-03-18 records the release of Open-Sora 1.0 with checkpoints. Its license at release is not shown in this packet.
Developer paper dated Dec 2024 documents text-to-video generation and public code and weights. It does not state the license.
Official Wan2.1 repo entry dated 2025-02-25 records the release of inference code and weights, with text-to-video models.
Same repo states an Apache 2.0 model license. This is the current page, not a release-day snapshot, but it completes the open-source criterion.

reviews.rationale: The forecast is supported. The early-resolution rule is met by dated releases: Open-Sora (March 2024, with code and weights) and Wan2.1 (Feb 2025, with code and weights under Apache 2.0) are public open-source text-to-video models released after the post. The sources are developer disclosures, but they document actual releases, which the contract accepts. No counterevidence was found.
